meta.name: tps-base
meta.description: TPS base profile. `extends: default` for the 18 security groups (deny_credentials, deny_keychains_*, deny_shell_*, dangerous_commands_*, system_*). Because `extends` appends and can never subtract, the TPS deny list below is re-stated explicitly instead of relying on inherited denies, and the system-write groups a TPS harness never needs are dropped by name (groups.exclude is the only subtraction). Linux note: Landlock cannot express deny-within-allow, so a deny nested inside an allowed parent makes nono refuse to start (it will not silently weaken the deny) — keep every deny at or above the allow roots. Matters for the exe.dev profiles (ops-mxf9). Never grant the state root: ~/.tps/secrets is a sibling of the mailbox and agent state, so a grant or deny at ~/.tps level takes the mailbox and agent state with it. The agent-side profile grants read on ~/.tps/identity at launch (the agent needs its own key); ~/.tps/secrets stays denied. /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers and /etc/ssh are denied explicitly so the broad system reads (system_read_macos / --read /etc) cannot reach them.
